title: Matching Shifted Parabola Equations to Graphs by Vertex Coordinates
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Match each parabola equation (a) y = (x - 1)^2 - 4, (b) y = (x - 2)^2 + 2, (c) y = (x + 2)^2 + 2, and (d) y = (x + 3)^2 - 2 to its corresponding graph in the figure, where Position 1 has vertex (2, 2), Position 2 has vertex (-2, 2), Position 3 has vertex (-3, -2), and Position 4 has vertex (1, -4).

steps.title: Identify the Vertex (h, k) from Vertex Form y = (x - h)^2 + k
steps.explanation: A parabola obtained by shifting y = x^2 horizontally by h and vertically by k has equation y = (x - h)^2 + k and vertex at (h, k).
steps.why: Since (x - h)^2 >= 0 vanishes uniquely at x = h, the minimum value k occurs at (h, k).

steps.title: Extract the Vertices for Equations (a) and (b)
steps.explanation: Equation (a) shifts y = x^2 right 1 and down 4 to vertex (1, -4), matching Position 4. Equation (b) shifts right 2 and up 2 to vertex (2, 2), matching Position 1.
steps.why: Matching the quadrant and coordinates of (h, k) uniquely identifies the shifted parabola.

steps.title: Extract the Vertices for Equations (c) and (d)
steps.explanation: Equation (c) shifts left 2 and up 2 to vertex (-2, 2), matching Position 2. Equation (d) shifts left 3 and down 2 to vertex (-3, -2), matching Position 3.
steps.why: Rewriting x + c as x - (-c) identifies a leftward horizontal shift to h = -c.
